# Introduction

The rapid growth of electric vehicle adoption presents both challenges and opportunities for power grid management. While EVs increase electricity demand, their batteries represent a distribured energy storage resource that could support grid stability through Vehicle-to-Grid technology. V2G enables bidirectional power flow allowing vehicles to send energy back to the grid during peak demand periods.

The challenge is in determining when V2G participation makes sense. Grid operators need power during specific high demand windows, but EV owners have different charging patterns, locations and battery states. Most exisiting V2G systems use simple time-of-use pricing rules that ignores these complexities, resulting in low participation rates and missed opportunities.

We address this gap by analyzing 72,856 real charging sessions from the Nature EV dataset, integration them with CAISO grid pricing data, and developing a scoring based decision engine. Key finding: Only 5.1% of sessions are V2G eligible under current conditions, but this can potentially increase to 12% through targeted engagement.

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section II details methodology. including data collection from both user session and grid source, preprocessing steps, and the decision engine architecture. Section III presents exploratory data analysis showing patterns in user behaviour. Section IV shows results including revenue calculations and EVerest integration outcomes. Section V discusses limitations and future direction.
